propositions: Parallel Git fetches against a shared common directory can race on remote-tracking ref updates, producing cannot lock ref compare-and-swap mismatches when uncoordinated processes observe refs changed by peer fetches
The sync fetch path in reconverge takes no cross-process lock and runs outside the store write lock; the snapshot fetch path locks only on snapshot-store and neither coordinates the other

Proof: controlled experiments with local repositories show 82 stale-reference failures in 128 parallel attempts but zero failures in 128 serialized attempts; snapshot and sync fetches against the same common directory produce 9 of 12 snapshot aborts and 113 of 132 sync failures in parallel but zero in serialized control

Bounded retry of ref CAS mismatches combined with a blocking cross-process lock keyed on the canonical Git common directory identity resolves the race while preserving the requirement that network fetches do not hold the ticket write lock
Production occurrences across multiple concurrent sessions and plan reviews demonstrate the defect is reproducible and affects both snapshot and sync paths identically
